title: Provenance Note on Crocheted Shell Handbag (Overview)
creator: Nicely, Patricia
description: Provenance note written by Patricia Nicely shortly after Pauline Elgar's death in 2003 and placed inside the crocheted shell handbag, reading: "this purse was made by the natives of Guam when Harold Dugan Elgar was stationed there during WWII. It was made from tiny shells which were found on beaches. The shells are very fragile and thinner than eggshells. They are pierced in two places with a fine bone needle and then crocheted together. The lining is made from parachute nylon. The handle and nameplate were made by Dugan Elgar. He was a chief in the Navy Seabees from 1943 to 1945, and was on the U.S. Island of Guam. The bag was given to his wife, Pauline Elgar, in 1944."
